Updated June 2026. If you are choosing an AI meeting assistant for your team in 2026, the answer turns on one question: do you want a bot to join your Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams call, or do you want recording and transcription to happen locally on the host's device? Full disclosure before we rank anything: Meetily is our product. It is built for bot-free, local-first recording (open source, 31,000+ GitHub stars, 599,000+ downloads as of September 2026), and it is not the right fit for everyone - if you need a mobile app or real-time cloud collaboration, one of the seven alternatives below will serve you better, and we say so where it applies. The AI meeting assistant market reached USD 3.67 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow at a 34.7% CAGR through 2034 (market.us AI Meeting Assistant Market report
(opens in new tab)
, 2025), and the meaningful 2026 differences are now data residency, consent, and per-seat cost - not "does it transcribe?".
We ranked 8 tools side by side on privacy, bot visibility, pricing, and platform support. Every claim below is anchored to verifiable numbers and primary sources.
Meeting notes software uses AI to automatically capture, transcribe, and summarize meetings. Modern AI meeting assistants go beyond simple recording to provide:
Automatic transcription - Speech-to-text conversion in real-time
Speaker identification - Who said what during the meeting
AI summaries - Key points extracted automatically
Action item detection - Tasks identified and assigned
Searchable archives - Find any meeting by keyword
The best meeting AI tools integrate with your calendar, video platforms, and productivity apps to create a seamless workflow.
AI Meeting Assistant vs Meeting Recorder

A meeting recorder simply captures audio/video. An AI meeting assistant goes further - transcribing, summarizing, identifying action items, and integrating with your workflow. Most tools in this guide are full AI meeting assistants, not just recorders.
Starting Price: Free (open source) | Pro from $10/user/month billed annually ($120/year)

Meetily is an AI powered meeting assistant that runs entirely on your local machine. No cloud uploads, no meeting bots - just private, AI-enhanced meeting notes. Community Edition is free, with Pro features available from $10/user/month.
100% local processing - meetings never leave your computer
AI transcription using Whisper or Parakeet engines
Cross-platform: Windows & macOS (Linux available via open source)

"When a meeting bot joins a privileged conversation, it becomes a third participant nobody invited. We built Meetily bot-free and open source so teams handling sensitive work can audit exactly what happens to their data, instead of taking a vendor's word for it."

-- Sujith S, CTO, Zackriya Solutions
Best For: Teams that handle sensitive information, compliance-focused organizations, and anyone who values data sovereignty over cloud convenience.
Limitations: No mobile app, collaboration requires file sharing (no cloud sync), requires decent hardware for real-time transcription.
The privacy-first AI meeting assistant that works offline.
Starting Price: Free tier | Pro from $16.99/month
Otter.ai pioneered the AI meeting notes space and remains a strong contender for real-time collaboration.
Integrates with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams
Best For: Teams that need real-time collaboration during meetings and don't have strict privacy requirements.

Limitations: All data stored on Otter's cloud servers, visible bot joins meetings, free tier has monthly limits, US-based servers may cause GDPR issues. Otter achieved HIPAA compliance on July 10, 2025
(opens in new tab)
, but the Business Associate Agreement is offered on Enterprise plans only - lower tiers cannot legally process Protected Health Information. See our full Meetily vs Otter.ai comparison for a side-by-side breakdown.
Starting Price: Free tier | Pro from $18/month
Fireflies.ai focuses heavily on sales and CRM integrations, making it ideal for revenue teams.
Automatic meeting summaries pushed to CRM
Best For: Sales teams that need meeting intelligence piped directly into their CRM without manual data entry.

Limitations: Visible "Fireflies.ai Notetaker" bot joins all meetings, cloud-only (no local option), learning curve for advanced features. Fireflies launched Fireflies for Healthcare in September 2025
(opens in new tab)
 with a HIPAA-compliant tier that requires an explicit BAA request - the default plans are not covered. See our Meetily vs Fireflies comparison for the full feature and privacy breakdown.
Starting Price: Free (25 meetings lifetime) | Individual from $18/month
Granola offers a clean meeting notes experience on Windows and Mac with AI enhancement and bot-free recording.
Bot-free - listens to device audio, no meeting bot
Polished native interface on Windows and Mac
Combines your manual notes with AI transcription
Note templates for sales, interviews, stand-ups
High transcription accuracy on clear audio
Best For: Note-takers who want a lightweight, bot-free meeting AI that enhances rather than replaces their note-taking style.

Limitations: Free tier is only 25 meetings total (lifetime, not monthly), cloud-based processing despite local capture, model training opt-out requires Enterprise tier ($35+/month), limited to 10+ languages. See our Meetily vs Granola comparison for open-source vs proprietary trade-offs.
5. Fathom (Best Free Option with Generous Limits)
Starting Price: Free (unlimited recordings) | Premium from $15-19/month
Fathom offers genuinely unlimited free recording and transcription, making it the most accessible meeting assistant ai.
Unlimited free recording, transcription, and storage (truly unlimited, not a trial)
AI highlights and video clips of key moments
5 AI summaries per month on free tier (unlimited on Premium)
Best For: Individuals and small teams who need robust meeting notes ai without paying, and don't have strict privacy requirements.

Limitations: Cloud-only processing, bot joins meetings (visible to participants), AI summaries limited to 5/month on free tier, advanced features require Premium upgrade after trial. Read our Meetily vs Fathom comparison for the privacy-first take.
Starting Price: Included with Microsoft 365 Copilot ($30/user/month)
Microsoft Copilot integrates AI meeting assistance directly into Teams.
Best For: Organizations already invested in Microsoft 365 ecosystem who want AI meeting without additional vendors.

Limitations: Expensive as add-on, only works in Teams (not Zoom/Meet), requires Microsoft 365 subscription, limited customization. See our Meetily vs Microsoft Copilot comparison for cross-platform alternatives.
7. Zoom AI Companion (Best for Zoom-First Teams)
Starting Price: Included with paid Zoom plans | Standalone $10/month | Cross-platform $12/user/month
Zoom's AI Companion 3.0 (released December 2025) has evolved into a sophisticated meeting assistant with agentic AI capabilities.
Cross-platform support now available (Teams, Meet, WebEx coming)
Federated AI using Zoom + OpenAI + Anthropic models
Best For: Teams that primarily use Zoom and want AI meeting features without managing another tool.

Limitations: Summaries sometimes misinterpret context (user reports), cannot learn company-specific terminology, cross-platform requires $12/month add-on, data processed on Zoom's servers. See our Meetily vs Zoom AI comparison for platform-agnostic options.
8. Read AI (Best for Analytics - With Caveats)
Starting Price: Free tier | Enterprise from $25/user/month
Read AI focuses on meeting analytics and engagement metrics, but comes with significant privacy concerns.
Meeting engagement scores and "Meeting Score" for participants
Best For: Team leads who want data-driven meeting insights and don't have strict privacy requirements.
Auto-joins meetings: Users report it joins without explicit consent after calendar sync
Privacy concerns: Mixed user reviews on TrustPilot citing privacy and consent issues
Analytics can feel intrusive to team members
See our Meetily vs Read AI comparison for a privacy-first take on meeting analytics.

Some organizations restrict meeting AI tools that upload data to external servers. If you work in education, healthcare, or government, verify your meeting notes software complies with institutional policies before deploying.

children.text: How to Choose the Right Meeting Notes Software
The biggest differentiator in meeting AI is where your data goes:
Why Privacy Matters for Meeting AI

Meeting recordings contain sensitive information: business strategies, client details, personnel discussions. Cloud meeting AI tools upload all of this to third-party servers. Even with encryption, you're trusting vendors with your most confidential conversations.
Not all meeting assistant ai tools support every platform:
Meeting notes software pricing varies dramatically:

children: Meetily (open source, unlimited), Fathom (unlimited recordings, 5 AI summaries/mo)
Otter Pro ($8-10/mo), Fireflies Pro ($10/mo), Fathom Premium ($15-19/mo)
Read AI Enterprise ($25/mo), Microsoft Copilot ($30/mo add-on)

children.text: Different tools excel at different workflows:
Solo professionals: Granola (Windows & Mac) or Meetily (any platform)

The release of efficient local AI models (Whisper, Parakeet) has made on-device meeting transcription practical. Local-first tools like Meetily now deliver high transcription accuracy entirely on-device, keeping data private.
Users are increasingly annoyed by visible "Notetaker" bots joining their meetings. Bot-free alternatives like Meetily and platform-native options (Copilot, Zoom AI) are gaining popularity.
Basic transcription is commoditized. The differentiator is now integration depth - how well does your meeting AI connect to CRM, project management, and productivity tools?

As more organizations scrutinize how meeting AI tools handle data, compliance and data sovereignty are becoming purchase criteria, not afterthoughts. Gartner predicts that more than 40% of AI-related data breaches will arise from cross-border GenAI misuse by 2027
(opens in new tab)
 (press release, February 2025), which puts pressure on procurement teams to prefer tools that keep transcripts inside controlled jurisdictions or on-device.

children.q: What's the best app for recording AND transcribing meetings in 2026?
children.a: It depends on whether a bot in the call is acceptable. If not, Meetily captures system audio locally on Windows or macOS, transcribes with OpenAI Whisper or Parakeet, and never adds a visible bot to your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call - Community Edition is free and open source under MIT; Pro is $10/user/month billed annually. If a visible bot is fine and you want zero setup, Fathom is the strongest cloud option with unlimited free recording plus transcription. Otter.ai and Fireflies also bundle recording with transcription and add real-time collaboration, but route audio through their cloud.

children.q: What's the best free AI meeting note taker for teams?
children.a: Two genuinely free choices stand out for teams in 2026. Meetily's Community Edition is fully free and open source (MIT) - with thousands of GitHub stars and a six-figure download count - offering local Whisper transcription, AI summaries, and bot-free recording. Fathom offers unlimited free cloud recording and transcription (AI summaries capped at 5/month on the free plan). Otter.ai and Fireflies have free tiers but cap them tightly (300 minutes/month on Otter Basic; 800 minutes/seat on Fireflies Free). For privacy-sensitive teams, Meetily is the only free option that keeps recordings on-device.

children.q: Read AI vs Granola: which should I pick in 2026?
children.a: Pick Granola if you want a polished, bot-free note-taker (Windows & Mac) that listens to device audio. Pick Read AI only if you specifically want meeting-engagement analytics and are comfortable with a visible bot that auto-joins from calendar sync. Granola: bot-free, hybrid local capture, $18/month individual, 25 free meetings lifetime. Read AI: cloud bot, engagement scores, free tier with caps, $25/user/month enterprise. If fully on-device processing matters more than either, a local-first tool like Meetily (free, open source) is also worth a look.

children.q: Which AI meeting assistants are most affordable for startups?
children.a: For lean startups, the most affordable AI meeting assistants in 2026 are: (1) Meetily Community Edition - free, open source, MIT-licensed, no per-seat fees; (2) Fathom Free - unlimited cloud recording and transcription with 5 AI summaries/month; (3) Meetily Pro - $10/user/month billed annually for speaker identification and advanced exports; (4) Otter Pro at $8-10/user/month on annual plans. Most expensive: Microsoft 365 Copilot at $30/user/month on top of an existing M365 subscription. If the team uses Mac and Windows, Meetily, Fathom, and Granola all run on both.

children.q: How do AI meeting assistants compare in 2026?
children.a: The 8-way 2026 comparison turns on four axes: bot visibility (Meetily and Granola are bot-free; Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, Read AI add a visible bot; Copilot and Zoom AI are platform-native), data location (Meetily processes locally; everyone else uploads to vendor cloud), price (Meetily Community is free, Pro is $10/user/month billed annually; Otter Pro $8-10/mo annual; Fireflies $10/mo; Granola $18/mo; Copilot $30/user/month), and platform reach (Meetily is cross-platform; Copilot is Teams-only; Zoom AI is Zoom-only). See the comparison table earlier in this guide for a side-by-side.

children.q: What is an AI note taker and how does it work?
children.a: An AI note taker is software that captures meeting audio and uses speech-to-text plus a language model to produce a transcript, summary, and action items automatically. Two architectures exist in 2026: (1) bot-based - the tool dials in as a visible participant (Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, Read AI) and uploads audio to vendor cloud; (2) bot-free local capture - the tool records system audio on the host's device (Meetily, Granola) and may transcribe on-device or in the cloud. Meetily runs the entire pipeline locally with OpenAI Whisper, so audio and transcripts stay on your machine unless you bring your own API key for the summary step.

children.q: Which meeting note tools have unlimited usage?
children.a: Truly unlimited in 2026: (1) Meetily Community Edition - no per-meeting, per-minute, or per-month caps because everything runs locally; (2) Fathom Free - unlimited cloud recording and transcription, but only 5 AI summaries per month on free, unlimited on Premium ($15-19/mo); (3) Meetily Pro - unlimited meetings included with the $10/user/month billed annually plan. Capped tools: Otter Basic (300 min/month), Fireflies Free (800 min/seat), Granola Free (25 meetings lifetime), Read AI Free (5 meetings/month). For organizations that record dozens of meetings per week, local-first processing is the only architecture with no metered ceiling, because there is no per-minute cloud cost to pass on.

children.q: What is the best meeting notes software in 2026?
children.a: The best meeting notes software depends on your priorities. For privacy and local processing, Meetily leads as an open-source AI meeting assistant. For enterprise collaboration, Otter.ai and Fireflies offer robust cloud features. For budget-conscious teams, Fathom provides unlimited free transcription.

children.q: Is there a free AI meeting assistant?
children.a: Yes, several options exist. Meetily's Community Edition is completely free and open source with core features included. Fathom offers unlimited free transcription (genuinely unlimited, not a trial). Otter.ai, Fireflies, and Read AI have free tiers with monthly limits. Microsoft Copilot is included if you already pay for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

children.q: What is the best meeting AI for privacy?
children.a: For privacy, the strongest architecture is local processing, and Meetily is the only tool in this comparison that runs the full pipeline on-device: audio and transcripts stay on your machine, and with local summarization it works completely offline - well suited to HIPAA and GDPR requirements. (If you bring your own API key, only transcript text is sent to your chosen provider for the summary step, and only if you choose that.) Among cloud tools, Granola keeps capture local but processes in the cloud; the rest upload audio to their servers.

children.q: Do AI meeting assistants join as bots?
children.a: Most do. Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, and Read AI all join meetings as visible 'Notetaker' bots that other participants can see. Meetily is bot-free - it records system audio locally without joining the meeting. Platform-native tools (Microsoft Copilot, Zoom AI) also avoid external bots.

children.q: Can meeting notes software work with Zoom, Teams, and Google Meet?
children.a: Most meeting notes software supports all major platforms. Meetily works with any platform because it captures system audio locally. Otter.ai, Fireflies, and Fathom have dedicated integrations for Zoom, Teams, and Meet. Microsoft Copilot only works in Teams, and Zoom AI only works in Zoom.

Yes, modern AI meeting assistants achieve high transcription accuracy on clear English audio. Meetily uses OpenAI Whisper which supports 99+ languages. Cloud tools like Otter.ai and Fireflies have similar accuracy. All tools struggle with heavy accents, background noise, or multiple overlapping speakers.

children.q: What meeting notes software is HIPAA compliant?
children.a: Meetily is HIPAA-compliant by design: transcription always runs locally on your device, so audio recordings and Protected Health Information are never transmitted for the recording step. For summaries, Meetily uses pluggable AI - choose local AI (Ollama or built-in models), or bring your own API key. For strict HIPAA workflows, Community Edition or local-only summarization keeps PHI entirely on-device with no BAA needed. Enterprise teams can request a BAA. Otter.ai achieved HIPAA compliance in July 2025 and Fireflies launched 'Fireflies for Healthcare' in September 2025, both on Enterprise plans with BAA requests required. Local processing with Meetily eliminates third-party PHI exposure entirely.

children.q: How much does meeting notes software cost?
children.a: Prices vary widely. Meetily Community is free (open source) with Pro at $10/user/month billed annually ($120/year). Fathom offers unlimited free recordings (AI summaries limited). Annual plans are typically 40% cheaper: Otter Pro ($8-10/mo), Fireflies Pro ($10/mo), Fathom Premium ($15-19/mo). Monthly rates are higher: Otter ($17/mo), Fireflies ($18/mo), Granola ($18/mo). Enterprise options like Microsoft Copilot add $30/user/month on top of existing M365 subscriptions.

The best meeting notes software in 2026 isn't one-size-fits-all. Your choice should balance privacy requirements, platform needs, budget, and workflow integration.

For privacy-conscious teams, Meetily's local AI approach offers something no cloud tool can match: complete data sovereignty. The trade-offs are real too - no mobile app and no cloud sync - so weigh them against your workflow.
For sales teams, Fireflies' deep CRM integration saves hours of manual data entry.
For budget-conscious individuals, Fathom's unlimited free tier is unbeatable.
For enterprise Microsoft shops, Copilot's native Teams integration minimizes friction.

The meeting AI landscape is maturing rapidly. Tools that seemed cutting-edge two years ago now face competition from local AI alternatives, platform-native options, and increasingly sophisticated open-source projects.

Choose based on what matters most to your organization. If privacy ranks high on that list, weigh local-first tools seriously; if real-time collaboration or mobile access ranks higher, a cloud tool is the honest answer.
